question: May a householder eat while neglecting dependents even in extreme distress?
premises: A householder has obligations to those he should support.
Abandoning them is a serious fault.
Even extreme personal distress does not justify eating in such neglect.
inference: A householder should not eat after abandoning his dependents, even if his life-breaths are at his throat.
uncertainties: The object of hitvā is implicit from context, likely parents or dependents.
plain_english: A householder should not eat after abandoning them, even when his life-breaths are at his throat.
